routes.label: Test the first possible forward counts

question: Greta Grasshopper sits on a long line of lily pads in a pond. From any lily pad, Greta can jump \(5\) pads to the right or \(3\) pads to the left. What is the fewest number of jumps Greta must make to reach the lily pad located \(2023\) pads to the right of her starting position?
solution:
Only the numbers of right and left jumps affect Greta's final position, because adding the jump distances in a different order gives the same sum. We can imagine making all the right jumps first, then correcting the overshoot with left jumps.

The right jumps must reach at least pad \(2023\), so at least \(405\) right jumps are necessary. Check the first possible landing points:

\[
\begin{array}{c|c|c}
\text{Right jumps}&\text{Landing pad}&\text{Overshoot}\\\hline
405&2025&2\\
406&2030&7\\
407&2035&12
\end{array}
\]

Each left jump removes \(3\) from the overshoot. The overshoots \(2\) and \(7\) cannot be removed by whole jumps, while \(12\) can, using \(12/3=4\) left jumps. Thus \(407\) right jumps and \(4\) left jumps reach the target.

Any larger feasible number of right jumps creates a larger overshoot and requires more left jumps too. So this first feasible case has the fewest jumps altogether:

\[
407+4=\boxed{411},
\]

choice \(\boxed{\text{D}}\).
